title: model-loading-breadcrumbs-harper-wong
notes:
Context:
- Investigating intermittent model load failures in dedicated pools when loading larger checkpoints for gptx-20b-v1. Failures are most common during cold starts and when autoscaler spins up multiple replicas concurrently.

Observed symptoms (recurring):
- Worker logs show repeated weight shard download failures during load:
  - "Shard download failed: HTTP 503 SlowDown"
  - "Checksum mismatch for shard weights-0003.bin (expected d2f3..., got 9a1b...)"
  - "Unexpected EOF while reading weights-0007.bin"
  - "Failed to parse checkpoint: unsupported header version 0x02" (only seen once)
- Approx 20% of attempts result in fallback to smaller variant (gptx-7b) as per auto-fallback policy.
- Customers report latency spikes and occasional 5xx errors for requests routed to freshly started machines.

Commands / diagnostic steps tried (timestamps local):
- Check object HEADs and metadata on S3 (failed run during spike):
  aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-models --key gptx-20b-v1/weights/weights-0003.bin
  -> HTTP 503 intermittently, sometimes returns with ETag but inconsistent Content-Length.

- Manual download to reproduce checksum mismatch:
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/gptx-20b-v1/weights/weights-0003.bin ./weights-0003.bin
  sha256sum weights-0003.bin
  -> result differs from baseline hash stored in manifest.json

- Range download test (to detect truncated objects):
  curl -r 0-1048575 -o part0.bin "https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-models/gptx-20b-v1/weights/weights-0003.bin"
  -> sometimes returns fewer bytes than requested (206 with smaller Content-Range).

- boto3 list and head checks inside failing node instance (python snippet):
  s3 = boto3.client('s3')
  obj = s3.head_object(Bucket='redwood-models', Key='gptx-20b-v1/weights/weights-0003.bin')
  print(obj['ContentLength'], obj['ETag'])
  -> Runs that succeed show expected size 1,073,741,824; failing runs either timeout or return smaller ContentLength.

- Verified manifest vs storage:
  cat manifest.json | jq '.shards[3].sha256'
  -> expected hash exists. Used small python script to stream-download and compute sha256 to compare.

Error snippets copied from logs:
- "2026-02-22T09:17:41Z ERROR weights_fetcher: shard weights-0003.bin download failed: HTTPError(503, 'SlowDown')"
- "2026-02-22T09:17:42Z WARN loader: checksum mismatch for weights-0003.bin expected= d2f3a1c... got=9a1b4f2..."
- "2026-02-22T09:17:42Z ERROR loader: aborting load, partial KV cache may remain"
- "2026-02-23T03:05:10Z ERROR weights_fetcher: Unexpected EOF while reading chunked body"
- "2026-02-23T03:05:11Z ERROR runtime: failing replica healthcheck due to model load failure"

Hypotheses / notes:
1) Storage-side throttling / S3 SlowDown (request rate against hot prefix)
   - Evidence: HTTP 503 SlowDown and variable Content-Length.
   - Counter-evidence: some nodes in same AZ succeed while others fail, which could still be bucket-side or networking.
2) Network/proxy causing truncation (corporate proxy / NAT gateway timing out)
   - Evidence: Unexpected EOF and partial range returns.
   - Counter-evidence: curl from the problematic host also sometimes succeeds; inconsistent behavior.
3) Race on multipart uploads / stale manifests: manifest lists shard sizes and hashes but a background reupload or repack could have left transient inconsistent objects.
   - Evidence: One-time "unsupported header version" error suggests a packaging mismatch.
4) Local disk/IO issues on instance (disk full, corrupted writes during streaming download)
   - Evidence: Partial files present in /tmp/ which are not cleaned and have smaller sizes.
   - Counter-evidence: checksum mismatch observed on freshly downloaded file before write completion detection.
5) Bug in downloader/parallel fetcher: e.g., overlapping range requests or incorrect boundary handling when combining parts leading to off-bytes and checksum mismatch.

Repro steps to run on a failing node (manual):
- kill -9 loader process to force fresh start
- remove /tmp/model-cache/gptx-20b-v1/*
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/gptx-20b-v1/weights/weights-0003.bin - | pv --bytes > /dev/null  # look for truncated stream
- python3 tools/compute_sha.py - <(aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/... -)  # stream hash check

Quick mitigations tried:
- Added exponential backoff with jitter around S3 get_object in weights_fetcher; reduced observed 503s but not eliminated.
- Temporarily increased allowed download retries from 3 -> 8 in instance image; reduced failures but still see checksum mismatch cases.
- Force-download to local disk and validate before loader continues (added atomic write + tmp->final rename). This eliminated one class of partially-written files but didn't remove intermittent truncated downloads.

Next actions / TODOs:
- Storage infra: open runbook and ask storage team to check bucket metrics (request count, slowdowns, throttling) and object PUT history for gptx-20b-v1 prefix (ACTION: Jordan).
- Reproduce from isolated bastion in same AZ with tcpdump to capture partial responses and look for resets (ACTION: me).
- Add more detailed HTTP logging (Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, bytes received) in weights_fetcher and enable at debug level for a week (ACTION: Maya to ship small PR).
- Validate multipart upload metadata and manifest generation pipeline for any async reuploads (ACTION: infra/model-ops).
- Temporarily change loader to validate object head (size+etag) before streaming and abort early if HEAD differs during download window (quick guard).
- If storage team confirms hot-prefix throttling, implement sharded prefixing and signed-url scatter-gather to reduce request concentration.

Notes for handoff to storage team (summary):
- Time windows: 2026-02-22 09:15-09:30 UTC and 2026-02-23 03:00-03:15 UTC show most evident failures.
- Objects: prefix gptx-20b-v1/weights/weights-*.bin. Examples: weights-0003.bin (1,073,741,824 bytes), weights-0007.bin (512,000,000 bytes).
- Symptoms: intermittent 503 SlowDown, truncated range responses, checksum mismatches, occasional unsupported header parse error.
- Steps already taken: increased retries, atomic write, more logging, temp guard on head-object.

Other context / related tickets:
- JIRA-INFR-2122: autoscaler creating N replicas causing spike of simultaneous downloads (possible root cause).
- GH-PR 876: atomic-write + retry changes (already merged to canary).

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is there a correlation between autoscaler burst behavior and specific availability zones? (need logs correlated with instance AZ).
- Are manifest generation jobs re-uploading shards shortly after initial upload?
- Could a CDN/caching layer between storage and instances be returning stale/incomplete responses?

If I don't update this doc, ping me in #eng-serving-runtime with "harper model-load breadcrumb".

Short checklist for follow-up meeting:
- [ ] Ask storage for request-rate metrics on prefix for the two failure windows.
- [ ] Run tcpdump + curl range test from failing AZs simultaneously.
- [ ] Increase debug logging and collect 24h of logs.
- [ ] Try alternate storage endpoint or presigned URL to validate permission/proxy differences.
